title: 4. Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L11: Web Security 2 (XSS · CSRF · Files · SSRF · API · Proactive Controls): 4. Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

items: Server fetches a URL the attacker controls → server becomes a confused deputy reaching internal resources
Attack surface: webhook URLs, "import from URL", PDF generators, image proxies, any param ending in _url

blocks.text: ``bash # AWS IMDSv1 — no auth required! http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role-name> # → returns AWS access keys → full cloud takeover ``

items: DNS rebinding: domain resolves to public IP first (passes check), then 127.0.0.1
Resolve hostname → check IP isn't private/loopback/link-local — block 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, 169.254/16 (AWS metadata!), fc00::/7
Disable unnecessary protocols — only https://; reject file://, gopher://, dict://
Use IMDSv2 on AWS — token-required model defeats SSRF→IMDS pivot
Network segmentation — webserver shouldn't reach metadata or internal admin services

blocks.text: Real-world: Capital One (2019) — SSRF on misconfigured WAF → AWS IAM credentials → 100M records, ~$80M cost. IMDSv2 + egress restrictions would have stopped the chain.
